# Branch review: `fix-checkpoint-trailer-block`

**Verdict: request changes**

Scope: `main...fix-checkpoint-trailer-block` at `2d16b3666`, covering one commit and seven changed files.

## Author intent

The change separates two meanings that the old checkpoint parser conflated:

- Whole-message parsing remains available for historical discovery, especially GitHub and native Git squash commits containing several embedded checkpoint trailers.
- Final-trailer-block parsing authorizes checkpoint creation, reuse, and mutation.

That split is the right design. The hook and attach changes apply it in several important places without breaking the existing squash-resume tests. The implementation is not complete, however: two mutation paths still trust whole-message results, and the strict parser does not match Git's trailer grammar.

No pull request currently exists for this branch. The related [PR #2168](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2168) remains open.

## Spec

### Act on

#### High: `checkpoint explain --commit ... --generate` can write to a body-selected checkpoint

[`runExplainAuto`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L617) and [`runExplainCommit`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L2994) still resolve commit linkage with whole-message `ParseCheckpoint`. When `--generate` is present, that ID reaches [`store.Write`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L1095).

A commit body can therefore name an existing but unrelated checkpoint and cause:

```text
commit body
    -> ParseCheckpoint(existing ID)
    -> checkpoint explain --generate --force
    -> generateCheckpointSummary
    -> store.Write(existing ID)
```

This violates the recorded requirement to "prevent untrusted checkpoint-shaped commit-body text from being accepted in unsafe contexts."

Use final-block parsing when commit resolution leads to summary generation. Keep whole-message parsing only for read-only discovery. Add regressions for both explicit `--commit` and positional commit fallback.

#### Medium: legacy migration still lets body text authorize reconciliation

[`migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded`](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_migration.go#L72) scans the whole message when a legacy state lacks `LastCheckpointCommitHash`. A matching body ID advances both `BaseCommit` and `AttributionBaseCommit`, skipping normal migration and changing future attribution.

This conflicts with the intended boundary that body IDs are discovery candidates while final-block IDs authorize mutation.

Require final-block evidence for the legacy fallback, or decline reconciliation when the recorded commit hash is unavailable. Add a legacy-state regression with a matching body ID followed by a different final trailer block.

### Consider

None.

### Noted

The existing squash-history semantics are preserved. All three named squash-resume unit tests passed unchanged.

### Dismissed

None.

**Worst spec issue:** `--generate` can persist a summary to a checkpoint selected solely by commit-body text.

## Standards

### Act on

#### High: leading whitespace turns body text into an authorizing trailer

[`ParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L162) and [`finalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L306) left-trim lines before classifying and parsing them.

This line is therefore accepted:

```text
  Entire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6
```

Git 2.50's `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns no trailer for the same message. The branch parser nevertheless lets that line choose the ID used by PostCommit condensation and attach.

Do not remove leading spaces or tabs when validating final-block trailer lines. Add production-path regressions for PostCommit and attach, not only parser tests.

#### Medium: commit-message comment handling does not follow Git configuration

[`parseCheckpointFromCommitMessageFile`](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go#L290) strips only `#` suffix lines. Git permits a configurable `core.commentChar`, and default cleanup preserves comment-prefixed lines when no editor runs. See the official [`git commit` cleanup documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit/2.52.0).

This creates two failure shapes:

- A repository using another comment character can hide a legitimate final trailer behind Git's comment block.
- A `git commit -m` or `-F` message can contain real `#` user content that this helper discards before deciding an earlier checkpoint-shaped body line is final.

Resolve Git's effective comment character or apply Git-equivalent cleanup rules. Cover editor, `-m`/`-F`, and custom-comment-character flows.

### Consider

#### Support Git trailer continuations

[`finalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L317) walks backward only while every line independently matches `Key: value`. Git accepts continuation lines beginning with whitespace, so a multiline trailer after `Entire-Checkpoint` can make the branch parser reject the entire block even though Git accepts it.

This may produce a duplicate checkpoint ID during prepare/amend or make PostCommit skip condensation. Either support continuation lines or explicitly document and test the narrower grammar.

#### Exercise attach through its durable boundary

`TestAttachIgnoresCheckpointShapedBodyText` calls `resolveCheckpointID` and `promptAmendCommit` separately. It does not prove through `runAttach` that a forged checkpoint remains unmodified and a fresh checkpoint receives the attached session.

A full-path regression should inspect the persistent store after attach.

### Noted

- The strict maintainability pass found no structural regression. The large hook file was already over 1,000 lines; this change did not cross that threshold or scatter the core parser policy.
- The parser change adds no lock or interruption point. Parser selection occurs before existing writes, so cleanup and recovery semantics are otherwise unchanged.
- Median `PrepareCommitMsg` time was 15.20 ms on this branch versus 15.13 ms on `main`, a difference of roughly 0.5% and within sample noise.

### Dismissed

One adversarial reviewer flagged `hasUserContent` for treating every checkpoint-shaped line as Entire metadata. That behavior predates this branch and requires a commit whose only user content is itself checkpoint-shaped. It is not a regression introduced here.

**Worst standards issue:** the strict parser accepts a Git-invalid indented body line as mutation authority.

## Correctness model

### Who owns each write?

- PrepareCommitMsg chooses the checkpoint ID; PostCommit owns condensation into persistent checkpoint storage.
- Attach chooses or reuses an ID, writes the attached session, then best-effort amends the commit.
- `checkpoint explain --generate` owns summary persistence.
- Session migration owns `BaseCommit` and `AttributionBaseCommit` reconciliation.

The first two owners now use the strict parser in their main paths. Summary generation and legacy migration do not.

### What happens around interruption?

The diff changes classification before existing writes. It does not add a lock, subprocess, temporary file, or new partial-write state. Existing write and recovery owners remain responsible before and after the decision. The outstanding risk is wrong-target mutation, not new interruption behavior.

### Which tests observe the real contract?

- The PrepareCommitMsg regression enters the production hook and would fail on the old code.
- The attach test observes helpers rather than the durable store contract.
- No regression covers body-selected summary generation, legacy migration, indented pseudo-trailers, custom Git comment characters, or trailer continuation lines.

## Multi-model agreement

Three independent reviewers examined the same intent and diff:

| Finding | Agreement | Disposition |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Explain generation trusts body IDs | 3/3 | Act on |
| Indented pseudo-trailer accepted | 2/3 | Act on |
| Legacy migration trusts body IDs | 2/3 | Act on |
| Git comment handling is hard-coded | 1/3 | Act on after local verification |
| `hasUserContent` removes body-shaped lines | 1/3 | Dismissed as pre-existing |

## Verification performed

- Focused trailer parser tests passed.
- Focused PrepareCommitMsg and attach tests passed.
- `TestFindCheckpointInHistory_MultipleCheckpoints` passed.
- `TestFindBranchCheckpoint_SquashMergeMultipleCheckpoints` passed.
- `TestResumeFromCurrentBranch_MultipleCheckpointsSaysLatest` passed.
- `git diff --check main..HEAD` passed.
- Git 2.50 rejected indented pseudo-trailers and accepted continuation-line trailer blocks in direct `git interpret-trailers --parse` checks.
- Checkpoint history records a successful pre-commit `mise run check`; the full gate was not rerun during this read-only review.

## Recommendation

Request changes. Close the two remaining mutation paths first, then make the strict parser agree with Git about indentation and comment cleanup. Preserve whole-message discovery for squash history throughout.

# General Review Lessons

- Make a guard's zero-match check count only the matches it is meant to protect. Matches that are always present, like the guard's own allowed cases, keep the check from ever firing.
- Test a guard by planting a violation and by breaking its detection, and see it fail both times. A guard that passes on clean code proves nothing.
- Before acting on a review finding, check whether existing tests or contracts explain the current shape. A structural test can be why the code looks the way it does.
- When code reads a user-owned config into a typed struct and writes it back, keep the fields it does not model. Any new reason to rewrite the file otherwise silently deletes user data.
- Make a new outer timeout longer than every internal budget on that path. Otherwise the kill fires before the code's own graceful fallback.
- Before setting an explicit timeout, look up the platform's current default for that exact event; an explicit value can shorten the budget rather than add one.
- When splitting known from unknown JSON keys to preserve them, decode only the exact known keys and keep every other key, case variants included, as unknown. `encoding/json` matches field names case-insensitively, so decoding the whole object lets a key like `"Command"` overwrite the real field.
- When a change makes a fix command riskier, changes which command to run, or adds a new place that reports an existing failure, check every place that already reports it (status, doctor, enable, help text) so they all give the same fix. Otherwise one screen sends people to the safe fix and the next to the destructive one, or one command prints the same failure twice with different fixes.
- When a test plants a failure to cover an error branch, make sure an earlier step doesn't fail first; otherwise the assertion passes without ever running that branch.
- Select an agent's final report by a marker it carries (such as the contract line), not by its position in the event stream; a trailing tool call or an empty message ID moves a position-based boundary.
- When code keeps state so a later run can retry, test the retry itself. A test that checks the kept state against the same expression the code uses would pass even if that expression were wrong.
- When decoding user-editable JSON into maps or pointers, skip null elements before writing to them; `[null]` decodes to a nil map and a write panics.
- Review a PR that is behind main against current main, not its own base: build both and run the same repro. Its tests pass on its old base even when keeping its side of a conflict would undo a fix merged since.
- When wiring user config into a new path, test it with a broken config too. A user rule that silently fails to load leaks the same way as one that was never wired.
- Make a fail-closed check fire only on the failure it guards against, not on a whole class of errors. A refusal on any settings error blocks unrelated cases and pushes users toward a less safe escape hatch, such as an unredacted `--raw` bundle.
- Read the Trail's current description and resolved findings before drafting review comments. The trail description can be newer than the PR description and may already list known follow-ups, which turns "you missed this" into a question about scale or timing.
- When a PR claims corpus validation, check what the corpus contained, and test on inputs from outside it, such as other languages and other codebases. A corpus drawn from one codebase can pass while common idioms elsewhere break.

// Scratch: commit.cleanup=scissors keeps lines above the scissors line as
// written, so Entire's "#" explanation stays in the recorded trailer paragraph.
func TestScratchScissorsCleanupCondenses(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
	testutil.RunGit(t, env.RepoDir, "config", "commit.cleanup", "scissors")
	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "config"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	env.AcceptGitConfigChanges(string(data))

	sess := env.NewSession()
	require.NoError(t, env.SimulateUserPromptSubmitWithPromptAndTranscriptPath(sess.ID, "change mine.txt", sess.TranscriptPath))
	env.WriteFile("mine.txt", "my agent work\n")
	sess.CreateTranscript("change mine.txt", []FileChange{{Path: "mine.txt", Content: "my agent work\n"}})
	require.NoError(t, env.SimulateStop(sess.ID, sess.TranscriptPath))
	env.GitAdd("mine.txt")

	// What git hands prepare-commit-msg under commit.cleanup=scissors.
	handed := "\n" +
		"# ------------------------ >8 ------------------------\n" +
		"# Do not modify or remove the line above.\n" +
		"# Everything below it will be ignored.\n" +
		"#\n" +
		"# On branch feature/test-branch\n"
	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(handed), 0o644))
	if out, err := env.prepareCommitMsgCmd(true, msgFile).CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
		t.Logf("prepare-commit-msg output: %s", out)
	}
	prepared, err := os.ReadFile(msgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	edited := "typed subject" + string(prepared)

	// git's scissors cleanup: cut at the scissors line, then whitespace cleanup.
	cut, _, _ := strings.Cut(edited, "# ------------------------ >8 ------------------------\n")
	stripspace := exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), "git", "stripspace")
	stripspace.Dir = env.RepoDir
	stripspace.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	stripspace.Stdin = strings.NewReader(cut)
	recorded, err := stripspace.Output()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	t.Logf("recorded message:\n%s", recorded)

	commitWithPostCommit(env, string(recorded))

	stamped := trailers.ParseAllCheckpoints(string(recorded))
	require.Len(t, stamped, 1, "prepare stamped one trailer")
	parse := exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), "git", "interpret-trailers", "--parse")
	parse.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	parse.Stdin = strings.NewReader(string(recorded))
	gitTrailers, err := parse.Output()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	t.Logf("git interpret-trailers --parse: %q", gitTrailers)
	require.True(t, advCheckpointStored(env, stamped[0].String()),

content.text:
**Verdict: request changes.** I reproduced one regression against main: under `commit.cleanup=scissors` (also `whitespace` or `verbatim`), an editor commit gets a trailer, but post-commit never writes its checkpoint. I haven't applied the /simplify cleanups yet; your working agreement says to wait for approval before editing.

## Brief

**What it does.** Only a commit's last trailer block, read the way git reads it, now decides which checkpoint the commit writes to. That covers prepare-commit-msg, post-commit, amend, attach and `explain --generate`. Read-only lookups still scan the whole message, because squash commits carry their trailers in the body.

The PR also:
- reads git's comment prefix (`core.commentChar`, `core.commentString`, `auto`);
- cuts the message only at the exact scissors line;
- accepts `Key:value` and tab-separated trailers;
- changes how commit-msg decides a message is empty;
- includes #2259's writer fix.

**Why.** An `Entire-Checkpoint:` line pasted, quoted or indented in the body could send a write into an unrelated checkpoint, or into one this clone hasn't fetched.

**Cost and risk.**
- Editor commits, amends and commit-msg each spawn one `git config` (about 3 ms). `-m` commits spawn none.
- The new reader is stricter than git in some message shapes. The PR calls that the safe direction, but for post-commit it isn't (finding 1).

**State.** Head is 4cfd66130 and CI is green. It merges cleanly with upstream/main f36367e6f, whose 3 newer commits don't touch these files. Both Copilot threads are resolved. No Trail exists for this branch, so there were no trail findings to check.

## Findings

### Act on

**1. High, regression: with `commit.cleanup=scissors`/`whitespace`/`verbatim`, the commit gets a trailer but no checkpoint.**
- In these modes git keeps `#` lines, so the commit records Entire's explanation lines inside the trailer paragraph:
  ```
  typed subject

  Entire-Checkpoint: 1e0ed969a3b4
  # Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above if you don't want to link ...
  # Last Prompt: change mine.txt
  # The trailer will be added to your next commit based on this branch.
  ```
- `git interpret-trailers --parse` still returns the trailer, because git skips comment lines inside a trailer block.
- [isTrailerBlock](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:440) rejects the whole paragraph, so [stampedTrailersOf](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_provenance.go:221) finds nothing and post-commit writes nothing. The same commit also breaks attach joining and `explain --generate`.
- Evidence: I ran a throwaway integration test through the real hooks (overlay only, nothing written to the repo). It fails on this branch and passes on upstream/main.
- Recommended fix: make the reader skip comment-prefixed lines inside and after the block, as git does. It needs the prefix at read time, and a spawn can be avoided when the message has no `Entire-Checkpoint` key. This covers all three modes and commits already recorded this way.
- Cheaper but partial alternative: write Entire's explanation in its own paragraph above the trailer. It misses `verbatim` when git's comment block is left in, and it misses existing commits.
- Add a scissors row to `TestTrailerAuthority_EditorCommitHonorsCommentChar`.

**2. Low-medium: every amend now spawns `git config` before any trailer or session check.** This is at [manual_commit_hooks.go:827](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:827); main spawned nothing there. Skip the spawn when `ParseAllCheckpoints(message)` is empty: every ID the last-block reader accepts also matches that regex. The agent fast path at `:2762` has the same pattern.

### Consider

**3. Low: CRLF scissors lines.** [isScissorsLine](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:180) accepts a CRLF scissors line, but git 2.50 doesn't cut there; I checked, and a CRLF-saved `commit -v` commit records the diff. So the comment "Git cuts only at that exact line" overstates parity. Either drop the `\r` tolerance and its test, or reword the comment.

**4. Follow-up: redo and squash inheritance still scan the whole message.** At [manual_commit_redo.go:69](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_redo.go:69) and [manual_commit_hooks.go:684](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:684), every ID found anywhere in a replaced or squashed commit's message is written into the new commit's last trailer block, which attach and `explain --generate` now trust. A body mention therefore becomes an authoritative trailer one hop later. The PR leaves this alone on purpose, so it's worth a line under "Known gap".

### /simplify: proposed, not applied

These keep behavior the same.
- **S1:** the spawn guard from finding 2.
- **S2:** [checkpointFromTrailerLine](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:155) is a second definition of "checkpoint trailer line" next to `checkpointTrailerLineRegex`. Use the regex so the remover and the readers can't drift apart.
- **S3:** [hasUserContent](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:313) repeats `StripEditorComments`'s comment-dropping loop. Call it when the message ends with git's comment block.
- **S4:** the "writer and readers share one grammar" note appears on both `appendTrailerLine` and `isTrailerBlock`. Keep it on `isTrailerBlock` only.
- **Tests:**
  - Use the existing `keepAll` instead of the new `keepAllTrailers`.
  - In `attach_test.go`, use the existing `readSummary` and `headCommitOf` helpers.
  - Pull the five copies of the prepare-hook run into one `runPrepareCommitMsg` helper.
  - Drop the "passes before and after" note from the `// GUARD:` comment at [checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go:240](cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go:240); it describes test history, which your comment rule excludes.

Skipped:
- removing `ParseCheckpointFromFinalTrailerBlock`: it mirrors the existing `ParseCheckpoint`/`ParseAllCheckpoints` pair, and removing it churns the tests;
- moving the prefix rules into one `trailers` function: depends on how finding 1 gets fixed;
- reading the config through go-git: it ignores includes and `git -c` overrides;
- bigger redesigns: a cleanup-mode type or a new mention API;
- the double deleted-list read in amend: under 0.1 ms.

## Verification
- **Regression test:** fails on the branch, passes on upstream/main.
- **Real git 2.50 checks:**
  - the scissors-mode commit's trailer is read by `interpret-trailers`;
  - a CRLF scissors line is not cut.
- **Focused tests, all passing:** the `trailers` and `strategy` packages, attach and explain tests in `cli`, and the trailer-authority, adversarial and checkpoint-delete integration tests.
- **Not rerun:** the full `mise run check` (CI is green on this head).

**Review lessons.** I checked the diff against `General.md` and `cli.md`; finding 3 also breaks your Agent Memory rule to state only verified behavior in comments. Proposed new lesson for `General.md`, not added: "When making a parser stricter for safety, check which way is safe for each caller. Rejecting input blocks a write you want to prevent, but it also silently drops a write you need, such as a checkpoint that a trailer git accepts points to."

I put a short version of these findings in the shared notes file `pr-2253-review.md`. The repository is unchanged.

paragraph. git's trailer parser skips those lines, but the final-block

The new tests failed before the fix because, in commit.cleanup modes other than the default, git keeps Entire's own `#` comment lines inside the commit, and the old reader rejected any trailer paragraph that contained them. Here's the walkthrough with the actual messages from the failing run.

**1. What git hands prepare-commit-msg with `commit.cleanup=scissors`.** In this mode git puts its whole comment block below a scissors line:
```

# ------------------------ >8 ------------------------
# Do not modify or remove the line above.
# Everything below it will be ignored.
```

**2. What Entire's prepare-commit-msg writes.** It inserts the trailer plus its explanation above the first `#` line:
```
Entire-Checkpoint: cf9aca16fd96
# Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above if you don't want to link ...
# Last Prompt: change mine.txt
# The trailer will be added to your next commit based on this branch.

# ------------------------ >8 ------------------------
...
```

**3. What git records.** Scissors mode cuts at the scissors line but keeps the `#` lines above it. The default `strip` mode would delete them, which is why this never showed up before:
```
typed in editor

Entire-Checkpoint: cf9aca16fd96
# Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above ...
# Last Prompt: change mine.txt
# The trailer will be added ...
```

**4. Why post-commit wrote nothing.**
- Post-commit asks "which checkpoint did this commit stamp?" and the old reader looked only at the last paragraph: those four lines.
- `isTrailerBlock` required every line to be a trailer or an indented continuation. `# Remove ...` is neither, so it rejected the whole paragraph and returned no trailer.
- With no stamped trailer, post-commit condensed nothing. Checkpoint `cf9aca16fd96` was never written, so `advCheckpointStored` was false: "post-commit must condense into the checkpoint the commit's trailer names."

**5. Why git still sees the trailer.** Git's trailer parser skips comment lines, so `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns `Entire-Checkpoint: cf9aca16fd96`. The test checks that first, to prove the commit really is linked by git's rules and the failure is in Entire's reader.

**The other rows:**
- **`whitespace`:** git also keeps its own `# Please enter the commit message…` block, so the last paragraph was pure comments and the old reader found no trailer.
- **`;` prefix:** same as the scissors row, with `;` lines.

**The other new tests:**
- **Attach test:** same cause. Attach read the last block, rejected it, and minted a new ID instead of joining: "attach wrote the session into 78219153be59, want the trailer's checkpoint a1b2c3d4e5f6".
- **Grammar unit cases:** with the prefix ignored, the 4 comment-line cases failed for the same reason.

**Why main passed:** main's post-commit scanned the whole message with a regex, so it found the trailer line no matter what followed it. This PR's stricter reader added the bug, and the fix makes it skip comment lines the way git does.

The two failures in `mise run check` were a different thing: 10-second timeouts in hook-install and external-agent tests under full-suite load. Both pass when run alone, and this PR doesn't touch either area.

1. An aborted editor amend gets committed with only the trailer (cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:206).

2. Typing on the blank line in the editor template loses the link (manual_commit_hooks.go:2917).
   - Mechanism: addCheckpointTrailerWithComment leaves only one blank line above the trailer. If the user types on that line, the subject runs straight into the trailer, e.g. subject\nEntire-Checkpoint: X.

content.text: Real git confirms the behaviors behind findings 2, 5 and 8. Next I'm classifying all eight and putting together the brief.

I checked all eight findings. Findings 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8 are regressions against main that this branch introduced (1 and 8 by the earlier commit-msg change, 2, 3 and 5 by the stricter final-block reader). Finding 4 is older and gets fixed with 1. Findings 6 and 7 behave the same as on main. Here's the evidence, then what I propose.

## What each finding comes to

| # | Real? | Regression vs main? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Aborted editor amend commits a trailer-only message | Yes | Yes, from the commit-msg change in 4cfd66130 | Restore, fresh-stamp and the agent fast path append the trailer after git's `#` block. commit-msg then sees a trailer as the last line, treats it as a `-m` message, and counts the `#` lines as content. |
| 2. Subject typed on the blank line above the trailer loses the link | Yes | Yes | The template is `\n\n` + trailer. Real git records `subject\nEntire-Checkpoint: X` as one paragraph (the subject), and `interpret-trailers` reads no trailer. Post-commit skips it; main's whole-message scan found it. |
| 3. `auto` plus scissors misreads the prefix | Yes, narrow | Yes | It needs `auto`, a comment-keeping cleanup mode, and a `#` line in the message. Prepare writes `;` lines inside the trailer paragraph, and the recorded-commit reader skips `#`. |
| 4. Restored amend trailer lost with `commit -v` | Yes | No, older | The same append-at-end lands below the scissors line. |
| 5. Reader stricter than git | Yes | Yes | Git 2.50 reads the trailer in a `cherry-pick -x` block (`(cherry picked from …)` line) and in a block that is at least 25% trailers and has a `Signed-off-by:`. Ours rejects both, so a `-x` cherry-pick acts unlinked while a plain cherry-pick acts linked. |
| 6. GitHub squash merge joins the last squashed checkpoint | Yes | No | Main's attach also took the last ID. By git's grammar that trailer is the commit's final block, so this rule can't tell the difference. |
| 7. `explain --generate` picks the first trailer, attach the last | Yes | No | Main's `ParseCheckpoint` also took the first. |
| 8. `commit.cleanup=strip` with `-m "#42 fix"` | Yes, narrow | Yes, from 4cfd66130 | Real git with `strip` drops the `#42 fix` line from an `-m` message too and records a commit containing only `Entire-Checkpoint: X`. Main's commit-msg removed the trailer, so git aborted. |

## Proposed fixes for this PR

Each fix gets a failing test first, through the real hooks where it can.

1. **Findings 1 and 4:** write the restored amend trailer, the fresh amend trailer and the editor fast-path trailer above git's comment block. The squash/redo helper already does this; I'd rename it to say what it does (`addCheckpointTrailerAboveComments`) and use it at those 3 sites. The commit-msg rule "a trailer at the end means `-m`" then holds again for everything Entire writes.
2. **Findings 2 and 3:** change the editor template to put the explanation above the trailer, each in its own paragraph:
   ```
   <subject line>

   # Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer below if you don't want to link …
   # Last Prompt: …
   # The trailer will be added to your next commit based on this branch.

   Entire-Checkpoint: X

   # Please enter the commit message…
   ```
   Typing on either blank line above can't run into the trailer, because the explanation and a blank line separate them. In scissors mode the explanation no longer sits in the trailer's paragraph, so finding 3 goes away without a special case for `auto`.
   - **Tradeoff:** a visible template change, and the text now says "below".
   - **Not fixed:** under scissors the explanation still ends up in the commit, as on main.
3. **Finding 5:** follow git's rule. A block also counts if it has a `Signed-off-by: ` or `(cherry picked from commit ` line and is at least 25% trailers. That's about 20 lines in `isTrailerBlock`, unit-tested against git's outputs first, and it makes `-x` cherry-picks behave like plain ones (and like main).
4. **Finding 7:** `explain --generate` takes the last final-block trailer, like attach. One line.

## Proposed to document, not fix

New "Known gap" sentences, text for your approval later:
- **Finding 6:** fixing it needs a separate way to recognize squash merges, and main behaves the same.
- **Finding 8:** a fix needs `commit.cleanup` plumbing plus a `git config` spawn on every `-m` commit (agents commit this way). It still can't see `git commit --cleanup=…`, and the case is a message made only of comment lines, which git itself would strip.

The alternative for 2 and 3: post-commit could trust the ID prepare stamped wherever it ends up, recorded in a marker the way inherited trailers are. That's more general but adds state, so I'd go with the template change. Nothing is edited yet.

Findings 1–5 and 7 are fixed locally (10 files, +385/−111). Each test failed before its fix and passes after. Nothing is committed, pushed or posted yet.

**What changed:**
- **Findings 1 and 4:** an amend's restored or fresh trailer, and an agent's editor-commit trailer, now go above git's comment block instead of after the diff.
- **Findings 2 and 3:** the editor template now writes Entire's explanation in its own paragraph above the trailer.
  - That change made a `commit.status=false` editor message end with the trailer, so commit-msg would have kept the trailer instead of aborting an untouched commit. commit-msg now treats Entire's explanation as the sign of an editor message. A guard test covers it.
- **Finding 5:** the reader follows git's rule for blocks containing a `Signed-off-by:` or cherry-pick note. The writer still joins only blocks that are pure trailers, so an existing #2259 test keeps its behavior.
- **Finding 7:** `explain --generate` takes the last trailer.
- **One more fix found while checking:** both writers used to insert before the *first* comment-prefixed line. An amend body or template with a `#` line mid-way then put the trailer above text git keeps, so it wasn't the final block. They now anchor to the comment block that ends the message, and two new unit tests cover it.

**Verification:**
- **Failing first:** `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (3 cases), `ClearedAmendMessageAborts`, `SubjectOnTheTemplatesSecondLineLinks`, the `auto` scissors row, the two `AnchorsToTheEndingBlock` tests, 3 grammar cases plus a writer case, and the explain test.
- **`mise run check`:** lint has 0 issues and 91 packages pass. Four tests in the hook-install and external-command-signal areas timed out under load. Each passes alone, and this PR doesn't touch either area.
- **Not covered:** `git commit --amend --no-edit` restoring a trailer into a message made *only* of `#` lines would put the trailer first. I left it, because it needs the restore path plus an all-comment message.

**Proposed commit message:**
```
fix(trailers): keep prepare's trailers in the block git reads

The final-block rule could still drop links the whole-message scan kept:

- An amend's restored or fresh trailer, and an agent's editor-commit
  trailer, were appended after git's comment block. commit -v cut them
  off with the diff, and commit-msg read the message as -m, so clearing
  an amend to abort it recorded a commit holding only the trailer. They
  now go above the comment block, as inherited trailers do.
- The editor template put the trailer right below the typing lines, so a
  subject typed on the second line joined it into the subject paragraph,
  which git never reads as trailers. Prepare's explanation now sits
  between them in its own paragraph, which also keeps the comment lines
  commit.cleanup=scissors leaves, in any prefix, out of the trailer
  block. commit-msg reads that explanation as the mark of an editor
  message, so an untouched commit.status=false message still aborts.
- The reader rejected blocks git accepts: a cherry-pick -x note, or
  other lines in a block with a Signed-off-by: line while trailers make
  up a quarter of it. It now follows git's rule; the writer still joins
  only blocks of trailers alone.

Both writers find git's comment block as the run of comment lines that
ends the message, so a "#" line in a kept body or a template no longer
pulls the trailer above lines git keeps. explain --generate writes into
the block's last trailer, the one attach joins, not the first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Proposed PR description changes:**

1. **Fix section, new paragraph** before "The commit-msg hook's empty-message check…":
   > Every trailer prepare adds to an editor message goes above the comment block that ends it, whether it is the template's, an amend's restored or fresh one, an agent's, or an inherited one, so `commit -v` cannot cut it off. The template puts prepare's explanation in its own paragraph between the user's lines and the trailer: a subject typed on the line just above cannot join the trailer into the subject paragraph, and cleanup modes that keep comments leave the trailer as its own block. Like git, the reader also accepts a block holding a `Signed-off-by:` or `(cherry picked from commit …)` line with other lines in it, while trailers make up at least a quarter of the block. `explain --generate` writes into the block's last ID, the one attach joins.
2. **The commit-msg paragraph in the same section:** replace "an editor message ends with git's comment block and a `-m`/`-F` message ends with its own text, so prefix lines count as comments only when that block ends the message," with:
   > an editor message ends with git's comment block or carries prepare's explanation, and a `-m`/`-F` message has neither, so prefix lines count as comments only in an editor message,
3. **Tests section, after the guards line:**
   > Review then found regressions in the stricter rule itself; these failed on the branch before their fix:
   >
   > - **Trailers prepare adds:** `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (amend restore, amend after a delete, agent editor commit), `ClearedAmendMessageAborts`, `SubjectOnTheTemplatesSecondLineLinks`, the `auto` row of `CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit`, and the `AnchorsToTheEndingBlock` unit tests. `UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` gains a `commit.status=false` guard.
   > - **Git's block rule and explain:** the cherry-pick and quarter-trailer cases in `trailers_test.go`, and `TestExplainGenerate_UsesTheLastFinalBlockTrailer`.
4. **Known gap, two new paragraphs** (findings 6 and 8):
   > A GitHub "Squash and merge" commit joins the squashed messages without indentation, so its final block is the last squashed commit's trailer and attach joins that checkpoint, as on main. Telling it apart needs a way to recognize squash merges.
   >
   > With `commit.cleanup=strip`, git also removes comment lines from a `-m` message, which commit-msg counts as kept, so `git commit -m "#42 fix"` is recorded with only its trailer instead of aborting. Fixing it needs `commit.cleanup` read on every `-m` commit, and `git commit --cleanup=…` would still go unseen.
